BLJU������/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`6��; ukai-jail native tier (macOS): defense profile.
; Template digest (SHA-256): b2ae082d8d41f393bdc5f83b3cc3f2e84a017b3a4aff68beeb81325c037dc5e4
; jail-macos §4.7 classes 1-4, jail-v2 §8.1 containment, jail-macos §4.10.
; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; --- Runtime baseline -------------------------------------------------------
; dyld ignition enumerates the root directory while locating the shared
; cache; without this every exec dies in dyld4::CacheFinder (measured).
(allow file-read-data (literal "/"))
; No kern.proc* grant: it would expose other processes' argv/environment.
; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")
    (sysctl-name "kern.argmax") (sysctl-name "kern.boottime")
    (sysctl-name "kern.maxfilesperproc") (sysctl-name "kern.maxprocperuid")
    (sysctl-name "machdep.cpu.brand_string") (sysctl-name "vm.loadavg"))
(allow file-ioctl (literal "/dev/dtracehelper"))
; Git opens /dev/null read-write and fails hard without the read half
; (measured with Homebrew's git).
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
; The read-only devices Linux's sandbox provides too: scripts read
; /dev/zero and /dev/urandom directly (`dd if=/dev/zero` was refused,
; measured). Reading them discloses nothing; writing stays denied.
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))
(allow system-socket)
; Creating a file needs file-read-metadata on the parent directory (measured:
; open(O_CREAT) stats the parent), which the read grants below carry for the
; granted trees. Reaching a granted tree through the root symlinks adds one
; more lookup: the symlink itself (K102's /var versus /private/var row), and
; runtimes that realpath every path (Node's module loader) lstat each
; ancestor component, so the chain above every granted root is readable as
; metadata only — names on the chain, never listings, never data. getcwd
; reads the cwd vnode, so a member whose working directory is a granted

; have no legitimate launchctl use, so executing it is denied outright,
; after the exec grants above (last match wins; exec is confined to the
; admitted read-only roots, so no other launchctl copy can run).

(deny mach-bootstrap)

; Template digest (SHA-256): b2ae082d8d41f393bdc5f83b3cc3f2e84a017b3a4aff68beeb81325c037dc5e4
; jail-macos §4.7 classes 1-4, jail-v2 §8.1 containment, jail-macos §4.10.
; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; --- Runtime baseline -------------------------------------------------------
; dyld ignition enumerates the root directory while locating the shared
; cache; without this every exec dies in dyld4::CacheFinder (measured).
(allow file-read-data (literal "/"))
; No kern.proc* grant: it would expose other processes' argv/environment.
; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")
    (sysctl-name "kern.argmax") (sysctl-name "kern.boottime")
    (sysctl-name "kern.maxfilesperproc") (sysctl-name "kern.maxprocperuid")
    (sysctl-name "machdep.cpu.brand_string") (sysctl-name "vm.loadavg"))
(allow file-ioctl (literal "/dev/dtracehelper"))
; Git opens /dev/null read-write and fails hard without the read half
; (measured with Homebrew's git).
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
; The read-only devices Linux's sandbox provides too: scripts read

(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))
(allow system-socket)
; Creating a file needs file-read-metadata on the parent directory (measured:
; open(O_CREAT) stats the parent), which the read grants below carry for the

; The system selection links, read as metadata (readlink): /bin/sh reads
; select/sh and otherwise prints "Error opening …" on every invocation;

BLJU������/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`6��; ukai-jail native tier (macOS): defense profile.
; Template digest (SHA-256): b2ae082d8d41f393bdc5f83b3cc3f2e84a017b3a4aff68beeb81325c037dc5e4
; jail-macos §4.7 classes 1-4, jail-v2 §8.1 containment, jail-macos §4.10.
; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; --- Runtime baseline -------------------------------------------------------
; dyld ignition enumerates the root directory while locating the shared
; cache; without this every exec dies in dyld4::CacheFinder (measured).
(allow file-read-data (literal "/"))
; No kern.proc* grant: it would expose other processes' argv/environment.
; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")
    (sysctl-name "kern.argmax") (sysctl-name "kern.boottime")
    (sysctl-name "kern.maxfilesperproc") (sysctl-name "kern.maxprocperuid")
    (sysctl-name "machdep.cpu.brand_string") (sysctl-name "vm.loadavg"))
(allow file-ioctl (literal "/dev/dtracehelper"))
; Git opens /dev/null read-write and fails hard without the read half
; (measured with Homebrew's git).
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
; The read-only devices Linux's sandbox provides too: scripts read
; /dev/zero and /dev/urandom directly (`dd if=/dev/zero` was refused,
; measured). Reading them discloses nothing; writing stays denied.
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))
(allow system-socket)
; Creating a file needs file-read-metadata on the parent directory (measured:
; open(O_CREAT) stats the parent), which the read grants below carry for the
; granted trees. Reaching a granted tree through the root symlinks adds one
; more lookup: the symlink itself (K102's /var versus /private/var row), and
; runtimes that realpath every path (Node's module loader) lstat each
; ancestor component, so the chain above every granted root is readable as
; metadata only — names on the chain, never listings, never data. getcwd
; reads the cwd vnode, so a member whose working directory is a granted
; root (the launcher sets it to the workspace) resolves its own position.
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/tmp") (literal "/var") (literal "/private") (literal "/"))
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/Library") (literal "/Library/Preferences") (literal "/System") (literal "/Users") (literal "/Users/admin") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app/Contents") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app/Contents/MacOS") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-parallel-02") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-parallel-02/data") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-parallel-02/data/attempts") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-parallel-02/data/attempts/att_8f7919c8-6992-4342-a8ba-e5e0f4275e53") (literal "/private") (literal "/private/var") (literal "/private/var/db") (literal "/usr") (literal "/var") (literal "/var/db"))

; The system selection links, read as metadata (readlink): /bin/sh reads
; select/sh and otherwise prints "Error opening …" on every invocation;
; xcode-select, every xcrun shim and the toolchain's own make read
; select/developer_dir and refuse to run without it (measured). Only the
; links: the selected toolchain stays ungranted until policy admits it,
; and an unadmitted selection fails loudly rather than falling back to
; another toolchain (xcode_select_link, the fallback, stays denied).
(allow file-read-metadata
    (literal "/private/var/select/sh") (literal "/private/var/select/developer_dir"))
; The workload forks and spawns pipelines; the child inherits the sandbox,
; so a fork starts no process outside it (§4.7 closes exec, not fork).
(allow process-fork)

; --- Filesystem: read-only admitted roots (jail-v2 §8.1) -------------------
(allow file-read* (subpath "/bin"))
(allow file-test-existence (subpath "/bin"))
(allow file-map-executable (subpath "/bin"))
(deny file-write* (subpath "/bin"))
(allow file-read* (subpath "/sbin"))

(deny process-exec (literal "/bin/launchctl"))
; mach-bootstrap stays denied as belt and braces for bootstrap-subset

(deny mach-bootstrap)
(deny mach-lookup)

; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")

    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")

; Template digest (SHA-256): b2ae082d8d41f393bdc5f83b3cc3f2e84a017b3a4aff68beeb81325c037dc5e4
; jail-macos §4.7 classes 1-4, jail-v2 §8.1 containment, jail-macos §4.10.
; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; --- Runtime baseline -------------------------------------------------------
; dyld ignition enumerates the root directory while locating the shared
; cache; without this every exec dies in dyld4::CacheFinder (measured).
(allow file-read-data (literal "/"))
; No kern.proc* grant: it would expose other processes' argv/environment.
; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")
    (sysctl-name "kern.argmax") (sysctl-name "kern.boottime")
    (sysctl-name "kern.maxfilesperproc") (sysctl-name "kern.maxprocperuid")
    (sysctl-name "machdep.cpu.brand_string") (sysctl-name "vm.loadavg"))
(allow file-ioctl (literal "/dev/dtracehelper"))
; Git opens /dev/null read-write and fails hard without the read half
; (measured with Homebrew's git).
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
; The read-only devices Linux's sandbox provides too: scripts read
; /dev/zero and /dev/urandom directly (`dd if=/dev/zero` was refused,
; measured). Reading them discloses nothing; writing stays denied.
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))
(allow system-socket)
; Creating a file needs file-read-metadata on the parent directory (measured:
; open(O_CREAT) stats the parent), which the read grants below carry for the
; granted trees. Reaching a granted tree through the root symlinks adds one
; more lookup: the symlink itself (K102's /var versus /private/var row), and
; runtimes that realpath every path (Node's module loader) lstat each
; ancestor component, so the chain above every granted root is readable as
; metadata only — names on the chain, never listings, never data. getcwd
; reads the cwd vnode, so a member whose working directory is a granted
; root (the launcher sets it to the workspace) resolves its own position.
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/tmp") (literal "/var") (literal "/private") (literal "/"))
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/Library") (literal "/Library/Preferences") (literal "/System") (literal "/Users") (literal "/Users/admin") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app/Contents") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app/Contents/MacOS") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-continue-01") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-continue-01/data") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-continue-01/data/attempts") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-continue-01/data/attempts/att_0fbe301c-8689-4fee-ac67-b74cb6857764") (literal "/private") (literal "/private/var") (literal "/private/var/db") (literal "/usr") (literal "/var") (literal "/var/db"))

; The system selection links, read as metadata (readlink): /bin/sh reads
; select/sh and otherwise prints "Error opening …" on every invocation;
; xcode-select, every xcrun shim and the toolchain's own make read
; select/developer_dir and refuse to run without it (measured). Only the
; links: the selected toolchain stays ungranted until policy admits it,

(deny process-exec (literal "/System/Library/CoreServices/RemoteManagement/ARDAgent.app/Contents/MacOS/ARDAgent") (literal "/bin/ps") (literal "/usr/bin/at") (literal "/usr/bin/atq") (literal "/usr/bin/atrm") (literal "/usr/bin/batch") (literal "/usr/bin/crontab") (literal "/usr/bin/login") (literal "/usr/bin/newgrp") (literal "/usr/bin/quota") (literal "/usr/bin/su") (literal "/usr/bin/sudo") (literal "/usr/bin/top") (literal "/usr/bin/write") (literal "/usr/libexec/authopen") (literal "/usr/libexec/security_authtrampoline") (literal "/usr/sbin/postdrop") (literal "/usr/sbin/postqueue") (literal "/usr/sbin/traceroute") (literal "/usr/sbin/traceroute6"))

; --- §4.7 class 2: asking another process to run something -----------------
; launchd job operations, LaunchServices and Apple Events are denied.
; mach-lookup is default-deny: only explicitly admitted services may be
; looked up, each justified by the backend evaluation (§4.10). Unix-domain
; sockets are default-deny apart from named grants, and network egress is
; denied except loopback to the attempt's two authenticated bridge ports.
(deny lsopen)
(deny appleevent-send)
(deny job-creation)
; Measured 2026-11-01 (macOS 27.0 build 26A428, SIP-disabled development
; VM): `(deny job-creation)` stops submit/bootstrap/load, but kickstarting
; a preloaded job still started it outside the sandbox and the job reached
; both custodians; `(deny mach-bootstrap)` changed nothing. Launchd consults
; the caller's sandbox only for job-creation, mach-lookup and mach-register
; (its audit-token checks), and SBPL v1 has no filter for Mach sends to the
; inherited bootstrap port, so no denyable operation names the kickstart
; route. The remaining profile-visible lever is the client binary: members
; have no legitimate launchctl use, so executing it is denied outright,
; after the exec grants above (last match wins; exec is confined to the
; admitted read-only roots, so no other launchctl copy can run).
(deny process-exec (literal "/bin/launchctl"))
; mach-bootstrap stays denied as belt and braces for bootstrap-subset
; operations; on this build it does not govern kickstart (measured above).
(deny mach-bootstrap)
(deny mach-lookup)

(deny network*)

BLJU������/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`6��; ukai-jail native tier (macOS): defense profile.
; Template digest (SHA-256): b2ae082d8d41f393bdc5f83b3cc3f2e84a017b3a4aff68beeb81325c037dc5e4
; jail-macos §4.7 classes 1-4, jail-v2 §8.1 containment, jail-macos §4.10.
; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; --- Runtime baseline -------------------------------------------------------
; dyld ignition enumerates the root directory while locating the shared
; cache; without this every exec dies in dyld4::CacheFinder (measured).
(allow file-read-data (literal "/"))
; No kern.proc* grant: it would expose other processes' argv/environment.
; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")
    (sysctl-name "kern.argmax") (sysctl-name "kern.boottime")
    (sysctl-name "kern.maxfilesperproc") (sysctl-name "kern.maxprocperuid")
    (sysctl-name "machdep.cpu.brand_string") (sysctl-name "vm.loadavg"))
(allow file-ioctl (literal "/dev/dtracehelper"))
; Git opens /dev/null read-write and fails hard without the read half
; (measured with Homebrew's git).
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
; The read-only devices Linux's sandbox provides too: scripts read
; /dev/zero and /dev/urandom directly (`dd if=/dev/zero` was refused,
; measured). Reading them discloses nothing; writing stays denied.
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))
(allow system-socket)
; Creating a file needs file-read-metadata on the parent directory (measured:
; open(O_CREAT) stats the parent), which the read grants below carry for the
; granted trees. Reaching a granted tree through the root symlinks adds one
; more lookup: the symlink itself (K102's /var versus /private/var row), and
; runtimes that realpath every path (Node's module loader) lstat each
; ancestor component, so the chain above every granted root is readable as
; metadata only — names on the chain, never listings, never data. getcwd
; reads the cwd vnode, so a member whose working directory is a granted

; sockets are default-deny apart from named grants, and network egress is
; denied except loopback to the attempt's two authenticated bridge ports.
(deny lsopen)

; a preloaded job still started it outside the sandbox and the job reached

; inherited bootstrap port, so no denyable operation names the kickstart
; route. The remaining profile-visible lever is the client binary: members
; have no legitimate launchctl use, so executing it is denied outright,
; after the exec grants above (last match wins; exec is confined to the
; admitted read-only roots, so no other launchctl copy can run).
(deny process-exec (literal "/bin/launchctl"))
; mach-bootstrap stays denied as belt and braces for bootstrap-subset
; operations; on this build it does not govern kickstart (measured above).
(deny mach-bootstrap)
(deny mach-lookup)

; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")

(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))

(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))

; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; --- Runtime baseline -------------------------------------------------------
; dyld ignition enumerates the root directory while locating the shared
; cache; without this every exec dies in dyld4::CacheFinder (measured).
(allow file-read-data (literal "/"))
; No kern.proc* grant: it would expose other processes' argv/environment.
; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")
    (sysctl-name "kern.argmax") (sysctl-name "kern.boottime")
    (sysctl-name "kern.maxfilesperproc") (sysctl-name "kern.maxprocperuid")
    (sysctl-name "machdep.cpu.brand_string") (sysctl-name "vm.loadavg"))
(allow file-ioctl (literal "/dev/dtracehelper"))
; Git opens /dev/null read-write and fails hard without the read half
; (measured with Homebrew's git).
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
; The read-only devices Linux's sandbox provides too: scripts read
; /dev/zero and /dev/urandom directly (`dd if=/dev/zero` was refused,
; measured). Reading them discloses nothing; writing stays denied.
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))
(allow system-socket)
; Creating a file needs file-read-metadata on the parent directory (measured:
; open(O_CREAT) stats the parent), which the read grants below carry for the
; granted trees. Reaching a granted tree through the root symlinks adds one
; more lookup: the symlink itself (K102's /var versus /private/var row), and
; runtimes that realpath every path (Node's module loader) lstat each
; ancestor component, so the chain above every granted root is readable as
; metadata only — names on the chain, never listings, never data. getcwd
; reads the cwd vnode, so a member whose working directory is a granted
; root (the launcher sets it to the workspace) resolves its own position.
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/tmp") (literal "/var") (literal "/private") (literal "/"))

; The system selection links, read as metadata (readlink): /bin/sh reads
; select/sh and otherwise prints "Error opening …" on every invocation;
; xcode-select, every xcrun shim and the toolchain's own make read
; select/developer_dir and refuse to run without it (measured). Only the

; Template digest (SHA-256): b2ae082d8d41f393bdc5f83b3cc3f2e84a017b3a4aff68beeb81325c037dc5e4
; jail-macos §4.7 classes 1-4, jail-v2 §8.1 containment, jail-macos §4.10.
; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; --- Runtime baseline -------------------------------------------------------
; dyld ignition enumerates the root directory while locating the shared
; cache; without this every exec dies in dyld4::CacheFinder (measured).
(allow file-read-data (literal "/"))
; No kern.proc* grant: it would expose other processes' argv/environment.
; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")
    (sysctl-name "kern.argmax") (sysctl-name "kern.boottime")
    (sysctl-name "kern.maxfilesperproc") (sysctl-name "kern.maxprocperuid")
    (sysctl-name "machdep.cpu.brand_string") (sysctl-name "vm.loadavg"))
(allow file-ioctl (literal "/dev/dtracehelper"))
; Git opens /dev/null read-write and fails hard without the read half
; (measured with Homebrew's git).
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
; The read-only devices Linux's sandbox provides too: scripts read
; /dev/zero and /dev/urandom directly (`dd if=/dev/zero` was refused,
; measured). Reading them discloses nothing; writing stays denied.
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))
(allow system-socket)
; Creating a file needs file-read-metadata on the parent directory (measured:
; open(O_CREAT) stats the parent), which the read grants below carry for the
; granted trees. Reaching a granted tree through the root symlinks adds one
; more lookup: the symlink itself (K102's /var versus /private/var row), and
; runtimes that realpath every path (Node's module loader) lstat each
; ancestor component, so the chain above every granted root is readable as
; metadata only — names on the chain, never listings, never data. getcwd
; reads the cwd vnode, so a member whose working directory is a granted
; root (the launcher sets it to the workspace) resolves its own position.
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/tmp") (literal "/var") (literal "/private") (literal "/"))

; The system selection links, read as metadata (readlink): /bin/sh reads
; select/sh and otherwise prints "Error opening …" on every invocation;
; xcode-select, every xcrun shim and the toolchain's own make read
; select/developer_dir and refuse to run without it (measured). Only the

BLJU������/usr/bin/sandbox-exec06��; ukai-jail native tier (macOS): defense profile.
; Template digest (SHA-256): b2ae082d8d41f393bdc5f83b3cc3f2e84a017b3a4aff68beeb81325c037dc5e4
; jail-macos §4.7 classes 1-4, jail-v2 §8.1 containment, jail-macos §4.10.
; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; --- Runtime baseline -------------------------------------------------------
; dyld ignition enumerates the root directory while locating the shared
; cache; without this every exec dies in dyld4::CacheFinder (measured).
(allow file-read-data (literal "/"))
; No kern.proc* grant: it would expose other processes' argv/environment.
; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")
    (sysctl-name "kern.argmax") (sysctl-name "kern.boottime")
    (sysctl-name "kern.maxfilesperproc") (sysctl-name "kern.maxprocperuid")
    (sysctl-name "machdep.cpu.brand_string") (sysctl-name "vm.loadavg"))
(allow file-ioctl (literal "/dev/dtracehelper"))
; Git opens /dev/null read-write and fails hard without the read half
; (measured with Homebrew's git).
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
; The read-only devices Linux's sandbox provides too: scripts read
; /dev/zero and /dev/urandom directly (`dd if=/dev/zero` was refused,
; measured). Reading them discloses nothing; writing stays denied.
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))
(allow system-socket)
; Creating a file needs file-read-metadata on the parent directory (measured:
; open(O_CREAT) stats the parent), which the read grants below carry for the
; granted trees. Reaching a granted tree through the root symlinks adds one
; more lookup: the symlink itself (K102's /var versus /private/var row), and
; runtimes that realpath every path (Node's module loader) lstat each
; ancestor component, so the chain above every granted root is readable as
; metadata only — names on the chain, never listings, never data. getcwd
; reads the cwd vnode, so a member whose working directory is a granted
; root (the launcher sets it to the workspace) resolves its own position.
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/tmp") (literal "/var") (literal "/private") (literal "/"))
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/Library") (literal "/Library/Preferences") (literal "/System") (literal "/Users") (literal "/Users/admin") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app/Contents") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app/Contents/MacOS") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-chain-01") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-chain-01/data") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-chain-01/data/attempts") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-chain-01/data/attempts/att_0220c998-13db-4807-879d-8d9e3946a28d") (literal "/private") (literal "/private/var") (literal "/private/var/db") (literal "/usr") (literal "/var") (literal "/var/db"))

; The system selection links, read as metadata (readlink): /bin/sh reads
; select/sh and otherwise prints "Error opening …" on every invocation;
; xcode-select, every xcrun shim and the toolchain's own make read
; select/developer_dir and refuse to run without it (measured). Only the
; links: the selected toolchain stays ungranted until policy admits it,
; and an unadmitted selection fails loudly rather than falling back to
; another toolchain (xcode_select_link, the fallback, stays denied).
(allow file-read-metadata
    (literal "/private/var/select/sh") (literal "/private/var/select/developer_dir"))
; The workload forks and spawns pipelines; the child inherits the sandbox,
; so a fork starts no process outside it (§4.7 closes exec, not fork).
(allow process-fork)

; looked up, each justified by the backend evaluation (§4.10). Unix-domain
; sockets are default-deny apart from named grants, and network egress is
; denied except loopback to the attempt's two authenticated bridge ports.
(deny lsopen)
(deny appleevent-send)

; VM): `(deny job-creation)` stops submit/bootstrap/load, but kickstarting
; a preloaded job still started it outside the sandbox and the job reached
; both custodians; `(deny mach-bootstrap)` changed nothing. Launchd consults
; the caller's sandbox only for job-creation, mach-lookup and mach-register
; (its audit-token checks), and SBPL v1 has no filter for Mach sends to the
; inherited bootstrap port, so no denyable operation names the kickstart
; route. The remaining profile-visible lever is the client binary: members
; have no legitimate launchctl use, so executing it is denied outright,
; after the exec grants above (last match wins; exec is confined to the
; admitted read-only roots, so no other launchctl copy can run).
(deny process-exec (literal "/bin/launchctl"))
; mach-bootstrap stays denied as belt and braces for bootstrap-subset
; operations; on this build it does not govern kickstart (measured above).
(deny mach-bootstrap)
(deny mach-lookup)

(deny network*)

BLJU������/usr/bin/sandbox-exec 6��; ukai-jail native tier (macOS): defense profile.
; Template digest (SHA-256): b2ae082d8d41f393bdc5f83b3cc3f2e84a017b3a4aff68beeb81325c037dc5e4
; jail-macos §4.7 classes 1-4, jail-v2 §8.1 containment, jail-macos §4.10.
; SBPL semantics measured on this build: the LAST matching rule wins, and
; filters match the resolved vnode (case- and spelling-insensitive).
(version 1)
(deny default)

; --- §4.7 class 1: direct control of another process -----------------------
; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on
; this build and are denied outright; task ports via mach-task-name and
; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
(deny process-info-dirtycontrol)
(deny process-info-ledger)
(deny mach-task-name)
(deny mach-task-read)

; --- Runtime baseline -------------------------------------------------------
; dyld ignition enumerates the root directory while locating the shared
; cache; without this every exec dies in dyld4::CacheFinder (measured).
(allow file-read-data (literal "/"))
; No kern.proc* grant: it would expose other processes' argv/environment.
; Hardware facts include libSystem's hw.pagesize_compat and Rust's
; hw.optional.* feature probes. Kernel facts remain explicitly enumerated.
(allow sysctl-read
    (sysctl-name-prefix "hw.")
    (sysctl-name "kern.osrelease") (sysctl-name "kern.osversion")
    (sysctl-name "kern.ostype") (sysctl-name "kern.version")
    (sysctl-name "kern.argmax") (sysctl-name "kern.boottime")
    (sysctl-name "kern.maxfilesperproc") (sysctl-name "kern.maxprocperuid")
    (sysctl-name "machdep.cpu.brand_string") (sysctl-name "vm.loadavg"))
(allow file-ioctl (literal "/dev/dtracehelper"))
; Git opens /dev/null read-write and fails hard without the read half
; (measured with Homebrew's git).
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
; The read-only devices Linux's sandbox provides too: scripts read
; /dev/zero and /dev/urandom directly (`dd if=/dev/zero` was refused,
; measured). Reading them discloses nothing; writing stays denied.
(allow file-read* (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/random") (literal "/dev/urandom"))
(allow system-socket)
; Creating a file needs file-read-metadata on the parent directory (measured:
; open(O_CREAT) stats the parent), which the read grants below carry for the
; granted trees. Reaching a granted tree through the root symlinks adds one
; more lookup: the symlink itself (K102's /var versus /private/var row), and
; runtimes that realpath every path (Node's module loader) lstat each
; ancestor component, so the chain above every granted root is readable as
; metadata only — names on the chain, never listings, never data. getcwd
; reads the cwd vnode, so a member whose working directory is a granted
; root (the launcher sets it to the workspace) resolves its own position.
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/tmp") (literal "/var") (literal "/private") (literal "/"))
(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/Library") (literal "/Library/Preferences") (literal "/System") (literal "/Users") (literal "/Users/admin") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app/Contents") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/Ukai.app/Contents/MacOS") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-exec-01") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-exec-01/data") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-exec-01/data/attempts") (literal "/Users/admin/ukai-compat-20261102/trials/k92-exec-01/data/attempts/att_871e82ba-574c-4c46-bab0-05610f13227e") (literal "/private") (literal "/private/var") (literal "/private/var/db") (literal "/usr") (literal "/var") (literal "/var/db"))

; The system selection links, read as metadata (readlink): /bin/sh reads
; select/sh and otherwise prints "Error opening …" on every invocation;
; xcode-select, every xcrun shim and the toolchain's own make read
; select/developer_dir and refuse to run without it (measured). Only the
; links: the selected toolchain stays ungranted until policy admits it,
; and an unadmitted selection fails loudly rather than falling back to
; another toolchain (xcode_select_link, the fallback, stays denied).
(allow file-read-metadata
    (literal "/private/var/select/sh") (literal "/private/var/select/developer_dir"))
; The workload forks and spawns pipelines; the child inherits the sandbox,
; so a fork starts no process outside it (§4.7 closes exec, not fork).
(allow process-fork)

; --- Filesystem: read-only admitted roots (jail-v2 §8.1) -------------------
(allow file-read* (subpath "/bin"))
(allow file-test-existence (subpath "/bin"))
(allow file-map-executable (subpath "/bin"))
(deny file-write* (subpath "/bin"))
(allow file-read* (subpath "/sbin"))
(allow file-test-existence (subpath "/sbin"))
(allow file-map-executable (subpath "/sbin"))

(deny lsopen)

; have no legitimate launchctl use, so executing it is denied outright,
; after the exec grants above (last match wins; exec is confined to the
; admitted read-only roots, so no other launchctl copy can run).
(deny process-exec (literal "/bin/launchctl"))
; mach-bootstrap stays denied as belt and braces for bootstrap-subset
; operations; on this build it does not govern kickstart (measured above).
(deny mach-bootstrap)
(deny mach-lookup)

; Signals by every route the vocabulary exposes, confined to the sandbox
; (the measured base). pid_suspend/pid_resume, memorystatus_control,
; priority changes and proc_rlimit_control have no same-sandbox filter on

; mach-task-read close ptrace/task_for_pid/task_name_for_pid for every
; target, members included. An explicit process-info denial is necessary
; alongside the sysctl allowlist: default-deny alone still permits
; KERN_PROCARGS2 on this build, exposing another process's environment.
(deny signal)
(allow signal (target same-sandbox))
(deny system-suspend-resume)
(deny system-memorystatus-control)
(deny system-sched)
(deny process-info*)
(allow process-info* (target self))
(deny process-info-setcontrol)
